newsitem.title: USA: Procter & Gamble Q4 share net up 13 pct.
newsitem.headline: Procter & Gamble Q4 share net up 13 pct.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co Thursday said strong sales growth lifted net earnings per share 13 percent in the April-June quarter to $0.87.
"We have had another very strong quarter of earnings and cash flow growth," chief executive John Pepper said.
"I am also particularly pleased with the acceleration in fourth quarter net sales and unit volume growth."

Net income was $611 million, a 10 percent increase over the same period in the prior year. Excluding unusual items in the prior year, net earnings per share and net income increased 16 percent and 13 percent, respectively.
The company said the higher per share growth reflects fewer shares outstanding.
Sales for the April-June quarter rose four percent over the year earlier period to $8.9 billion.
Excluding the impact of currency translation, sales for the quarter would have been up seven percent. Volume grew six percent to a new quarterly record.

For the year ended June 30, earnings per share were a record $4.87, a 14 percent increase over the prior year. The company also had record net earnings of $3.42 billion, a 12 percent increase over fiscal 1996.

The difference between sales and unit volume growth was primarily due to product mix, lower pricing in laundry and lower commodity-based paper pricing. Excluding the 1996 gain on the sale of its health care joint venture stake, the North America's earnings rose eight percent to $2.30 billion.

The company said the region achieved this growth through unit volume progress and a continued focus on simplification, and standardization. Laundry detergents and fabric conditioners continued to drive the region's unit volume progress. The Food and Beverage sector, aided by new snacks production capacity, and the Paper sector also contributed to the volume gain.

P&G said Europe, Middle East, and Africa unit volume grew seven percent for the year, generating about one-half of the company's total volume growth. Sales grew 1 percent to $11.58 billion. The difference between sales and unit volume growth primarily reflects unfavorable exchange rates and lower commodity-based paper pricing.

It said the region's earnings grew 20 percent to $857 million, driven by volume growth and cost control, generated through simplification and standardization efforts. Central and Eastern Europe and the Middle East and Africa led the region's unit volume growth.
Results in the Asia region were mixed, P&G said. The region had a seven percent decline in unit volume for the year. Sales for the region were down eight percent to $3.57 billion.

Improved pricing and product mix were offset by the impact of unfavorable exchange rate movements. Weak unit volume results reflected the move to Efficient Consumer Response (ECR) and softness in Japan, which was partially offset by double digit volume growth in the Philippines and Indonesia.
The company said ECR introduced value pricing and simplified trade terms to reward efficiency of trade customers and eliminate inefficient promotional spending.
"This strategic move followed our experience in the United States where a similar program had some negative short-term impacts, followed by significantly improved longer-term growth."
The region's earnings were $274 million, an 8 percent increase over 1996, and reflected simplification and standardization efforts and the divestiture of non-strategic brands.

Unit volume for the Latin America region was down 2 percent, as the region continues to be impacted by economic difficulties and a slower than anticipated recovery in consumption levels, P&G said. However, sales in the region grew 6 percent to $2.30 billion as inflation-driven pricing action more than offset the effects of lower volume. Earnings for the region were $217 million, a four percent increase.

The company said its operating cash flows reached a record $5.9 billion in 1997, an increase of about 40 percent over 1996, reflecting the benefit of the simplification and standardization programs. Over the last three years, operations have generated over $13 billion in cash flow, providing the ability to fund dividends, capital programs, the share repurchase program and acquisitions.
((-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610))
